proposal.name: Drain a watcher before restarting it

plan.name: Drain a watcher before restarting it
plan.summary: Add an idempotent, nonblocking Factory.Drain() and wire SIGUSR1 to it for watch, registering and acknowledging the signal from command startup and remembering an early request; SIGTERM, Ctrl-C and context cancellation retain their existing cancellation behavior. Draining closes admission to new agent operations, including already queued drafts of statements, plumbing plans and issue plans and modeled or plumbing builds, without recording a run or reporting deferred work as failed; admitted operations finish with their checks, reviews, fallbacks, repairs, result recording and publication intact. While those steps finish the watcher continues polling, heartbeats, commands, ratifications, merges, closure handling and lease renewal, then promptly stops dispatching, joins its remaining steps and renewal, releases only its own lease through the existing bounded cleanup and returns successfully, allowing a waiting successor to take the lease on its next poll and continue from the completed build without rerunning it. Update SPEC.md with decision-cited drain behavior, README.md with a brief drain-and-restart pointer, and docs/factory.md with SIGUSR1 usage, cancellation behavior and a restart procedure that drains and waits before replacing the binary or reusing its work directory, explaining that overlapping watchers need separate work directories. This is tested plumbing built on #422 and #455, preserving D-0069, D-0113, D-0237 and D-0300; the merger must record the new drain decision, which has not yet been recorded, with SPEC and documentation maintained under D-0122 and D-0294.

tests.name: TestDrainFinishesBuildsAndKeepsQuickSteps463
tests.says: With full or spare agent capacity, draining defers queued and new drafts and builds without run records or failure posts, continues commands, ratifications, merges and heartbeats, preserves its active build, and exits successfully with the build recorded and published and its lease released.

tests.name: TestDrainRenewsLeaseAndHandsBuildToSuccessor463
tests.says: A draining watcher renews its lease through a long build, excludes a second watcher until its steps finish, then a waiting watcher takes the released lease without waiting for expiry and merges the completed build exactly once without another agent run.

tests.name: TestDrainWakesIdleAndWaitingWatchers463
tests.says: An idle, already-drained or lease-waiting watcher exits successfully on drain without waiting for its poll timer, and never relinquishes another watcher's lease.

tests.name: TestCancellationStillStopsADrainingWatcher463
tests.says: Context cancellation during draining still cancels active work, joins pending steps and releases the lease without starting a queued agent.

tests.name: TestWatchAcceptsSIGUSR1AsGracefulDrain463
tests.says: The actual watch command accepts SIGUSR1 from startup as a graceful drain, either exiting successfully when idle or acknowledging the pending drain, and still unwinds normally on SIGTERM while a drain is pending.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and five acceptance tests covering graceful draining, continued quick work, lease renewal, and successor handoff. Check 1 passed: all tests fail on the baseline as required, and `repo/` remains unchanged.
